dossier.title: Lot's visitors and the crowd: Genesis 19 and Qur'an 11
dossier.historical_background: Genesis' Sodom narrative belongs to the Abraham-Lot cycle. The Qur'an recasts the scene as a prophetic warning and rescue narrative; direct literary dependence is unproven.
dossier.comparison: Both describe visitors, a hostile crowd, Lot's hospitality and his daughters. Genesis describes a meal, Lot's foreigner status and the angels blinding attackers; Qur'an foregrounds Lot's distress, the crowd's lack of claim on his daughters, and his appeal for strong support.
dossier.chronology_caveat: Composition, redaction, textual tradition, and surviving manuscript dates must be distinguished. Compare Masoretic Hebrew with Greek Septuagint and relevant Jewish interpretation before verification.
